prompt: Which of these does `stored.py`'s card record beside the model? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A fingerprint of the training data
choices.why: Yes, `sha256`.

choices.text: The source code of `churn_model.py`
choices.why: The code is the one thing it does not hold.

choices.text: The first and last month learned from
choices.why: Yes, `from` and `to`.

choices.text: The library versions
choices.why: Yes, which `load` compares.

prompt: Why is lesson 15's pipeline the model worth serving, rather than a model that needs its columns prepared first?

choices.text: It has the highest AUC of the course
choices.why: It does not; lesson 8's boosters do better.

choices.text: Pipelines cannot be fitted again
choices.why: `load_model.py` fitted one again.

choices.text: It takes the raw table
choices.why: Yes. Otherwise every caller holds a second copy of the preparation.

choices.text: joblib can only save objects that come from scikit-learn's pipeline module
choices.why: It saves almost any Python object.

prompt: How many bytes did the saved logistic pipeline take on disk?
`load_model.py` printed `identical: True`. What did it compare?

choices.text: The weights of two logistic regressions
choices.why: It compared what they predict.

choices.text: The card's sha256 and the data's
choices.why: It printed the fingerprint; it did not compare it.

choices.text: The two files on disk, byte by byte
choices.why: There is one file; the other model was fitted fresh.

choices.text: Two models' chances
choices.why: Yes, all 13,154, to the last bit.

prompt: Loading the model from `/tmp` failed with `No module named 'churn_model'`. Why?

choices.text: The file names code that could not be imported
choices.why: Yes. It holds `churn_model.add_shapes` as a name, not as code.

choices.text: The file was damaged by the move
choices.why: It loaded fine from `~/ml`.

choices.text: joblib files only open in the folder they were saved in
choices.why: The path was given in full; the problem is the code.

choices.text: The versions on the card did not match
choices.why: That raises `RuntimeError` from `stored.load`; this was `joblib.load` directly.

prompt: A colleague finds a churn model online as a `.joblib` file and wants to load it to compare. What does the lesson say?
hint: Loading imports what the file names.

choices.text: Load it in `/tmp`, where it cannot reach anything
choices.why: A folder is no protection; the code runs as you.

choices.text: Not unless you trust its author with your machine
choices.why: Yes. A stranger's model file is a stranger's program.

choices.text: Fine, since a model file is data
choices.why: It is a program as much as data.

choices.text: Fine, as long as the versions written on its card match ours
choices.why: Versions say nothing about what code it runs.

prompt: Why does `app.py` describe every field of a subscriber, with types and ranges?

choices.text: To make the model faster
choices.why: It changes nothing about speed.

choices.text: The pipeline needs pydantic objects rather than tables
choices.why: The request is turned back into a table.

choices.text: The model trusts its input, so the door must check
choices.why: Yes. An age of −3 would get a confident chance.

choices.text: FastAPI refuses to start without it
choices.why: An endpoint can take a plain dictionary.

prompt: `rating_90d: float | None = Field(ge=1, le=5)` has no default. What does that allow?

choices.text: A request may leave the field out
choices.why: Leaving it out gave `Field required`.

choices.text: Any number, since the range is only advice
choices.why: The range is enforced.

choices.text: A rating of 0 for no rating
choices.why: 0 is below the range and is refused.

choices.text: `null` if sent; refused if missing
choices.why: Yes. A known gap and a forgotten field look different.

prompt: Why are `plan` and the other word fields typed as plain `str` rather than a list of known values?

choices.text: A list would refuse the monthly plan
choices.why: Yes. The cost is that typos are accepted too.

choices.text: Words do not matter to the model
choices.why: Payment and plan matter, lesson 19 showed.

choices.text: JSON has no way of sending a word
choices.why: It sends strings all the time.

choices.text: Pydantic cannot check against a list
choices.why: `Literal` does, as `app_user` shows.

prompt: What HTTP status did the server give the request with an age of `"forty"`?
C00007 was sent with `plan` set to `daily`, a plan that does not exist. What happened?

choices.text: It got the same chance as the weekly plan
choices.why: It fell from 0.6449.

choices.text: Scored as an unknown plan, 0.3843
choices.why: Yes. The encoder gave it zeros.

choices.text: The server crashed
choices.why: It answered 200.

choices.text: It was refused with 422
choices.why: `plan` is any string, so it passed.

prompt: To start the server for `app.py`, the second terminal runs `uvicorn ___:app`.
Where does `app.py` keep every answer it gives?

choices.text: In the card
choices.why: The card describes the model.

choices.text: Nowhere; the answer goes only to the caller
choices.why: Each is appended to a file.

choices.text: In `scores.jsonl`
choices.why: Yes, with the time and the model's name.

choices.text: In `uvicorn.log`, beside the request lines
choices.why: That shows requests and statuses, not chances.

prompt: What is training–serving skew?

choices.text: The server answering more slowly than the batch it replaced
choices.why: Slow is not wrong.

choices.text: A model fitted on old months
choices.why: That is lesson 22's drift.

choices.text: Unequal class sizes
choices.why: That is lesson 13.

choices.text: The served and measured models disagreeing on a case
choices.why: Yes, usually from the road in rather than the model.

prompt: A client sends 0 for `days_since_login` when the subscriber has no app. Why does that lower their chance?

choices.text: To the model, 0 means logged in today
choices.why: Yes. Mean chance 0.071 to 0.065, six credits lost.

choices.text: 0 is refused and replaced by the median
choices.why: 0 is inside the range and accepted.

choices.text: The server rounds small numbers away
choices.why: It rounds chances to four places, nothing else.

choices.text: Zeros are ignored by logistic regression
choices.why: A zero is a value like any other.

prompt: How would anybody notice the client sending 0 instead of null?

choices.text: From the 422s in the server log
choices.why: Nothing was refused.

choices.text: A row-by-row comparison with the batch it was measured on
choices.why: Yes. Nothing else shows it.

choices.text: The chances would look implausible to a reader
choices.why: Every answer was a plausible number.

choices.text: The model raises a warning
choices.why: It cannot know what the client meant.

prompt: Which of these is a reason `app.py` is not yet a service the retention team can rely on?

choices.text: It writes a log
choices.why: The log is the most important file it writes.

choices.text: FastAPI cannot run in production
choices.why: It does, with workers and a process manager.

choices.text: It answers anybody

choices.text: Its chances are not calibrated

prompt: A colleague upgrades scikit-learn on the server and restarts it. With `stored.load`, what happens?

choices.text: It refits the model on the new version
choices.why: Nothing refits automatically.

choices.text: Nothing, since versions only matter for training
choices.why: They matter to whatever the file names.

choices.text: It starts and answers with slightly different chances
choices.why: `stored.load` stops it before that.

choices.text: It refuses to start, naming both versions
